questions.question: What is pattern matching in Java?
options: Checking an object's type and extracting a value in a single expression
A design pattern for creating objects
A way of matching with regular expressions
explanations: Correct. Pattern matching allows checking an object's type and binding it to a variable in a single expression, avoiding explicit casting.
It is not a creational design pattern.
It is not for regular expressions (that is Pattern from java.util.regex).
It is not a parallel programming technique.

questions.question: What does switch do with pattern matching?
options: case String s: checks the type and extracts the value into the variable 's'
Only compares exact values as before
Ignores the type and only compares values
Throws an exception if the type does not match
explanations: Correct. In switch with pattern matching, a case like case String s checks the type and binds the value to the variable 's'.
With pattern matching it goes beyond comparing exact values.
It does not throw an exception; it simply does not enter that case.

questions.question: What is instanceof with pattern matching?
options: It allows writing if (obj instanceof String s) to check the type and extract the value
Only checks the type without being able to extract the value
It is the same as traditional instanceof
explanations: Correct. With pattern matching, instanceof can bind the value to a variable, avoiding a subsequent cast.
It can extract the value and bind it to a variable.
It is more powerful than traditional instanceof.
It works with any type, not just abstract classes.

questions.question: What is a sealed class?
options: A class that can only be extended by a known set of classes
A class that cannot be modified after being compiled
A class with all private attributes
A class that implements the Serializable interface
explanations: Correct. A sealed class restricts which classes can extend it using the permits clause.
It has nothing to do with immutability after compilation.
It is not just about private attributes.
It is not related to Serializable.
